name: Cloud
description: The minimal-agent cloud connector. It owns the network transport to the cloud backend and registers that transport in the host transport registry. Thus the Intercom peers and teams span machines, and Intercom does not import this plugin. Skeleton: the remote transport is a stub (no live connection) until the backend auth contract lands. Tool: CloudStatus.

tool.name: CloudStatus
tool.description: Show the status of the minimal-agent cloud plugin. The tool shows if the cloud functions are on, the cloud flags, and if the network transport is in the transport registry of the harness. Each use also adds that transport to the registry. A second use does not change the registry. At this time, the network functions of the transport do not operate. For example, `CloudStatus({})`.

format.description: The output format. The default is `"text"`.

tool.name: CloudLogin
tool.description:
Log this CLI in to the minimal-agent cloud backend with the OAuth device-authorization flow (RFC 8628). The tool shows a short user code and a URL. The user opens the URL in a browser and gives approval for the code. Then the tool completes the login and saves the access token on this computer. After the login, these cloud functions start: teleport, and peers and teams on other computers.

To set the backend, set `MINIMAL_AGENT_CLOUD_URL`. The default is `http://localhost:4000/api/auth`. For example, `CloudLogin({})`.

tool.name: CloudPush
tool.description:
Upload the new records of this session to the cloud teleport store immediately. Then the user can see the session live on the web or on a mobile device. The tool sends only the records that the cloud did not receive. Thus you can use the tool again safely, and an upload continues after a stop.

The tool operates only after a login with `CloudLogin`, and only when the cloud functions are on. If not, the tool does not upload records. The upload also starts automatically in the background between turns. For example, `CloudPush({})`.
